headline: Poland is using an AI system that combines camera and drone feeds to watch part of its border with Belarus.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a real deployment, but the system was announced in July and the update gives no results or numbers.
importance_line: Border guards and soldiers get software that flags events so fewer people stare at screens, and migrants crossing from Belarus are more likely to be spotted; the trial covers only a few dozen kilometres and no results are reported.
summary: The Defence Blog reports that Poland’s Operational Command says its “Intelligent Border” AI system is working as part of Operation Safe Podlasie, being tested on a stretch of the Belarus border several dozen kilometres long. The software recognizes objects, judges what they are doing and flags events for human operators, aiming to cut the hours soldiers and border guards spend watching video.
notes: Full article read. System announced in July 2026 with operational use planned for August; the article does not date the command’s latest statement.
